Class MKCScreenHandler

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.screen.MKCScreenHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.PanelOwner
public class MKCScreenHandler extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu implements com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.PanelOwner
The structural heart of MenuKit. Holds the Panel tree, owns the flat slot list, owns the bidirectional coordinate mapping, and handles shift-click routing and visibility transitions.

Proper subclass of AbstractContainerMenu — vanilla's sync machinery traverses this.slots and anything that breaks instanceof Slot breaks the world.

Implements PanelOwner so Panel can notify on visibility changes without depending on this class directly.

  • Field Details

    • PANEL_NOT_FOUND

      public static final int PANEL_NOT_FOUND
      Sentinel returned by getPanelButtonId(String) when no panel matches the requested id. Callers must guard against this before passing the result into clickMenuButton / handleInventoryButtonClick — a raw -1 would send a bogus button id over the wire. Named so the not-found case is explicit at every call site rather than buried in an unexplained magic number.

  • Constructor Details

    • MKCScreenHandler

      protected MKCScreenHandler(net.minecraft.world.inventory.MenuType<?> type, int syncId, List<com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.Panel> panels, Map<String, List<SlotGroup>> groupsByPanel)
      Constructs a handler from a pre-built panel list and a map of slot groups keyed by panel id.

      Allocates MKCSlots in declaration order: for each panel, for each of its slot groups (as supplied in groupsByPanel), for each slot index. Flat indices are sequential.

      Parameters:
      type - the menu type
      syncId - the sync id
      panels - the ordered panel list (each Panel holds only elements)
      groupsByPanel - map from panel id to the list of slot groups attached to that panel, in declaration order

    • getGroupsFor

      public List<SlotGroup> getGroupsFor(String panelId)
      Returns the slot groups attached to the panel with the given id, in declaration order. Returns an empty list if the panel has no slot groups (element-only panel) or the id is unknown.

      Slot groups are inventory-menu machinery and live on the handler rather than on Panel — Panel is context-neutral across all three rendering contexts. Callers that need "which slot groups belong to this panel" go through this accessor.

    • getGroupContaining

      public SlotGroup getGroupContaining(int flatIndex)
      Returns the SlotGroup that owns the given flat slot index, or null if the index is out of range or not a MenuKit slot.

      Reverse lookup: flat index → group. Useful for consumers that need to identify group membership from a slot index (e.g., shift-click preview, analytics).

    • findGroupForSlot

      @Internal public Optional<com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.SlotGroupLike> findGroupForSlot(net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot)
      Finds the SlotGroupLike that a slot belongs to, fast-pathing MenuKit-owned slots and delegating to MK's recognition for observed vanilla slots.

      Per §0043 (Complete-on-Side Feature Ownership), this is the MKC-side facade for combined owned + observed lookup. Consumer mods with a MKCScreenHandler in hand call this for the fast-path; consumer mods working only against vanilla handlers call MK's static HandlerRecognizerRegistry.findGroup(AbstractContainerMenu, Slot) directly.

      Parameters:
      slot - the slot to look up
      Returns:
      the owning group (owned fast-path or observed recognition), or empty if no group contains the slot
      Implementation note:
      Internal plumbing. Takes a raw vanilla Slot; its only caller is the library's contract verification. Consumers reach a group by panel id (getGroupsFor(String)) or by the stable handler-local flat index (getGroupContaining(int)), not by handing back a raw Slot.

    • quickMoveStack

      public net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack quickMoveStack(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, int index)
      Three-layer declarative shift-click routing.
      1. Identify source group. If it doesn't export, return EMPTY.
      2. Collect candidates: groups that import, can accept the stack, and are visible (not inert).
      3. Order by: directional pairing first, then source-aware baseline, then declared priority descending.
      4. For each candidate: merge into partials, then fill empties.
      5. Stop when stack is consumed.

    • builder

      public static MKCScreenHandler.Builder builder(net.minecraft.world.inventory.MenuType<?> menuType)
      Creates a builder for declaratively constructing a MKCScreenHandler. 
      // Mod-init: declare attachments via M7's StorageAttachment.
public static final StorageAttachment<BlockEntity, NonNullList<ItemStack>> CHEST_EXTRA =
    StorageAttachment.blockScoped("my-mod", "chest_extra", 9);
public static final StorageAttachment<Player, NonNullList<ItemStack>> POCKETS =
    StorageAttachment.playerAttached("my-mod", "pockets", 27);

// Menu construction: bind attachments to owner instances. Groups are
// structure-only; arm any slot behavior (e.g. an upgrade-only gate) by
// Address at init via Window.slot(address).set(MKCBehaviorKeys.GATING, gate).
MKCScreenHandler.builder(MY_MENU_TYPE)
    .panel("main", p -> p
        .group("container", CHEST_EXTRA.bind(blockEntity))
        .group("player", POCKETS.bind(player)))
    .panel("upgrades", p -> p
        .group("slots", EphemeralStorage.of(4))
        .hidden())
    .build(syncId)

      Namespace your panel ids

      A created slot's Address is global, keyed by (panelId, groupId, localIndex) — NOT scoped by the owning MKCMenu's Identifier. So two mods (or two menus) that both name a panel "main" share an address sub-space and would arm each other's slots. Namespace each panel id per-mod — e.g. "mymod:menu:main" — exactly as container-parity panel ids already are. The same id is used both for layout references (rightOf / below / pairsWith) and for addressing the panel's created slots (MKCScreenHandler.address(panelId, groupId, i)), so one namespaced id covers both concerns.

    • address

      public static com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.Address address(String panelId, String groupId, int localIndex)
      THE canonical Address of one slot in a custom-menu group declared on this handler's builder — use it to name a custom-menu slot when arming behavior or reading per-slot state by address. The custom-menu twin of MKCContainerPanel.address(String, String, int) (which is for container-parity define() slots): a custom-menu slot carries the bare declared panel id (no ":groupId" derivation), so this applies the right encoding for you. Prefer it over the now-@Internal CreatedSlotAdapter.addressOf, which mints a non-resolving address if handed the wrong path's id. 
      Window.slot(MKCScreenHandler.address("mymod:menu:side", "filtered", i))
      .set(MKCBehaviorKeys.GATING, gate);
      Parameters:
      panelId - the panel id declared on the builder (.panel(panelId, ...))
      groupId - the slot group id within that panel
      localIndex - the slot's index within its group
